claims.answer: Everything is local or user-hosted: state lives in ~/.dev3.0 (JSON) with hourly backups, board copy can be exported into the project, conversations dump to JSON; no vendor account or service is needed; headless mode self-hosts the UI.

claims.answer: Code, prompts, logs and artifacts stay on the machine except what the chosen agent CLIs send to their providers. Release builds send anonymous analytics to Google Analytics 4 and PostHog (no names, paths, prompts or diffs) with one switch, DEV3_TELEMETRY=off or DO_NOT_TRACK=1; a build from source has no PostHog key.

sources.title: Install guide
sources.locator: macOS desktop; Windows zip; WSL; Linux; tmux; Cloud VM caveats
sources.finding: macOS app via Homebrew cask or DMG; Windows x64 zip (brand new, unsigned, auto-update not proven); Linux headless CLI with glibc 2.28+, tmux required; WSL topology.

sources.title: Remote access
sources.locator: How the connection works; Background lifecycle; Keeping the box up to date
sources.finding: dev3 remote serves the full UI to any browser via Cloudflare quick tunnel, LAN or SSH forward; signed one-time URL (65 s) then 8-hour trusted session; backgrounds as a service; systemd unit; self-update.

sources.title: Agent support matrix
sources.locator: Agents table; Managed restart and hibernation; Feature Matrix; hooks per agent
sources.finding: Dedicated adapters for Claude Code, Cursor Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi, plus generic CLI; hooks drive status for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot; session resume per agent.

sources.title: Integrations page
sources.locator: Built-in agent support; Any other CLI tool; Model backends
sources.finding: dev-3.0 does not ship its own model or host agents; it launches installed CLIs under the user's accounts; Claude Code and Codex can use Amazon Bedrock; any CLI can be configured with no hooks or resume.

sources.title: Board-view extensions
sources.locator: The folder; dev3-extension.json; consent
sources.finding: Extensions add board views (not sandboxed, consent at install); ship as a folder with manifest and ES module.

sources.title: State backups

sources.title: Troubleshooting

sources.finding: dev3 doctor checks install health and reclaims worktree disk on request.

sources.title: Contributor and architecture guide

sources.title: Decision records

sources.title: Start-after scheduler

sources.title: Automations scheduler

sources.title: Remote access server

sources.finding: Single HTTP and WebSocket server serving the UI, RPC at /rpc and PTY proxy at /pty.

sources.title: Keep-alive scheduler

sources.finding: Auto-revives a task's agent when its process exits and gives up after bounded attempts.

sources.finding: Registered outside agents can message tasks and read replies from an inbox, with approvals.

sources.title: GitHub PR status

sources.finding: Shows PR number and live CI state on cards via gh.

sources.title: System memory probe

sources.title: Bounded search: native issue tracker and external trackers
sources.locator: grep -Ei linear|jira|github issues over src/bun, src/cli, docs/integrations
sources.finding: No Linear, Jira or GitHub Issues integration in the application; README says to integrate through the agent's own MCP. Tasks are native board cards.

sources.title: Bounded search: users, roles and SSO
sources.locator: grep -Ei saml|oidc|sso|rbac|organization|membership across src and docs
sources.finding: No multi-user accounts, roles or SSO: README says the unit is the individual, not the org.

sources.title: Bounded search: managed cloud and mobile apps
sources.locator: grep -Ei vendor cloud|managed|ios app|android app|testflight across src and docs; ls docs/install.md headings
sources.finding: No vendor cloud and no native phone app; phone use is the browser UI through dev3 remote.

sources.title: Bounded search: living specifications
sources.locator: grep -Ei living spec|requirements|product spec|drift across README, docs, src
sources.finding: No persistent requirements or drift-detection feature; per-task notes, overview and project config only.

sources.title: Bounded search: MCP server and API
sources.locator: grep -Ei mcp server|rest api|http api over src/bun, src/cli
sources.finding: dev-3.0 exposes no MCP server or public HTTP API; control is the dev3 CLI over a local socket and the remote web UI RPC.

sources.title: Bounded search: spend, token and time limits
sources.locator: grep -Ei max budget|spend limit|token limit|timeout over src/bun and agent-support-matrix
sources.finding: No product-wide spend, token or time cap; per-agent max budget is passed to agents that support it; usage and limit readings are informational.

sources.title: Bounded search: release, deploy, rollback, revert and delivery evidence
sources.locator: grep -rniE 'rollback|revert|deploy|release notes|gh release|gallery|stale.*approv|invalidat|screen record' over src, docs and README.md, excluding translations, tests, ideas and changelogs
sources.finding: No release, deployment, rollback, revert, recording, preview-gallery or approval-invalidation feature found. Matches are unrelated: a git reflog regex that treats 'revert' as work-producing, terminal-state rollback prototypes, one skill-text mention of deploy targets and settings galleries for fonts and shell prompts; screenshot matches are the show-image viewer and dev-server log notes.

sources.title: Outbound notification transports
sources.locator: NotificationTransport type (kind exec | webhook), runWebhook, notifications.json config
sources.finding: A user-configured notifications.json lists transports; a webhook transport POSTs the task notification event as JSON (with optional headers) and an exec transport runs a command with the event on stdin. Absent config the path is inert.

sources.title: Remote access: notifications that reach you when nothing is open
sources.locator: Notifications that reach you when nothing is open; A command or webhook
sources.finding: Documents ~/.dev3.0/notifications.json with transports of kind webhook (POSTs the event JSON to a URL with optional headers) and exec, plus Web Push to a phone browser.
